lead: This is an analysis tool, not a promise of profit. Always compare the hit rate with what the market already expected: hitting lots of bets the market already rated as very likely is no credit to the model.

intro.highProbability: <bold>High probability:</bold> at most one selection per match, when the model gives it at least 62% and at least 3 points more than the market. It combines pre-match odds, Dixon-Coles and each team's patterns. In 25/26 and 26/27 it hit 74.8% when the market expected 68.5%, but in the three previous seasons (22/23–24/25) it hit 68.7%, exactly what the market expected. It hits a lot because it picks likely selections, not because it knows more than the bookmakers.
intro.value: <bold>Value (EV):</bold> selections where Dixon-Coles gives a higher probability than the odds. They hit less often (they include away wins and draws) and are judged by ROI, not hit rate.

emptyHighProbability: No high-probability selections for the upcoming matches. The model needs pre-match odds (scripts/refresh_odds.py and then refresh_predictions.py), and in many matches no selection clears both thresholds: that's expected, not an error.
emptyValue: No value recommendations yet for matches still to be played: calculating EV requires real market odds. Load the pre-match odds (scripts/refresh_odds.py) and generate the predictions again. In the meantime, use ‘Your odds’ on each match page to compare your own odds with the model.

column.evTitle: Only in 1X2 and Over/Under 2.5, which have real odds in the data

history.empty: No settled recommendations yet on matches already played for this filter.

note.highProbability: High-probability model selections over 25/26 and 26/27, calculated with a model trained only on earlier seasons and with thresholds fixed before seeing these matches. <bold>The margin over the market is the measure of merit</bold>, not the hit rate: always choosing what the market rates as most likely also hits a lot, and loses money. ROI only counts 1X2 and Over/Under 2.5, the only markets with real odds in the data. Misses are never left out of this list or these calculations.
note.value: Selections the model flagged as value (positive EV) in matches already played. <bold>ROI is the measure that matters, not the hit rate on its own</bold>: a low-probability selection (e.g. an away win at 15%) is expected to lose most of the time even with genuinely positive EV. Misses are never left out of this list or these calculations.
